correctness.rationale: From cited linked-net component theorem and diagonal Chow-class degree, there are h one-dimensional components with an h-by-h nonnegative projection-degree matrix whose columns each sum 1 and rows each are positive, hence it is a permutation matrix: all components are distinct coordinate lines. Normal-crossings excludes triple points; any cycle in the dual graph forces a repeat node because all other components on the cycle have constant coordinate in the omitted factor, hence no cycles. The cited eventual Hilbert polynomial 1+sum d and nodal normalization Euler characteristic show h-1 nodes, so the forest is connected. Leaf removal and evaluation surjectivity on P1 give H^1=0 and h0=1+sum d for every d>=0. The ambient restriction correction uses the leaf-varying factor vanishing at the shared constant coordinate and matches any discrepancy of degree d_v vanishing at the node. Hilbert series/K polynomial are then algebraic consequences. The existing Cartwright–Sturmfels diagonal-Hilbert-scheme theorem supplies embedded smoothing for such a connected coordinate-line tree. The finite script checks six trees/684 multidegrees but does not verify every linked net or constitute the universal proof.
